title: Sum Root to Leaf Numbers
prompt:
Each root-to-leaf path in a binary tree represents a number formed by concatenating the digits along the path (each node's value is a single digit from 0 to 9). Given the `root` of such a binary tree, return the total sum of all root-to-leaf numbers.

The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from it, so you only need to compute the sum.

examples.explanation: The path 1->2 represents the number 12, and 1->3 represents 13. Total: 12 + 13 = 25.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [1, 1000]
The depth of the tree does not exceed 10
hints: As you move down from the root, you can build the number incrementally: each step, multiply the running number by 10 and add the current digit.
A completed root-to-leaf number is only counted once you reach a leaf node (no children) — that's when you add the running total to the overall sum.
Pass the accumulated number so far down through the recursion as a parameter, updating it before recursing into each child.

solution.approach: DFS from the root, carrying an accumulated number formed so far (starting at 0). At each node, update the accumulated value as accumulated * 10 + node.val. If the node is a leaf, this accumulated value is a complete root-to-leaf number, so add it to the running total. Otherwise recurse into both children with the updated accumulated value.
